findings.title: SQL Injection in php-plain/order_detail.php:6 via GET parameter 'id'

evidence.why: Source: User input from GET parameter
Sink: User input concatenated directly into SQL query without sanitization or binding

findings.attack_scenario: A crafted 'id' parameter can alter the WHERE clause logic, allowing access to other users' orders or bypassing intended filters.
findings.impact: Unauthorized data access; potential for reading, modifying, or deleting arbitrary data accessible by the database user.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) instead of string concatenation.

findings.title: SQL Injection in php-plain/search.php:8 via GET parameter 'q'

evidence.why: Source: User input from GET parameter
Sink: Input appended to SQL string. 'addslashes' is insufficient for SQL injection prevention in this context.
Sink: Unsanitized 'sort' parameter concatenated into dynamic ORDER BY clause (High Risk).

findings.attack_scenario: A crafted 'q' parameter can break the LIKE clause or inject logic; a crafted 'sort' parameter can alter execution order or access columns.
findings.impact: Authentication bypass, data manipulation, or information disclosure depending on DB privileges.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries for the search term and implement a strict allow-list validation for the 'sort' parameter.

findings.title: SQL Injection in php-plain/search.php:9 via GET parameter 'sort'

evidence.why: Source: User input from GET parameter
Sink: Unsanitized 'sort' variable concatenated into dynamic ORDER BY clause. No allow-list or binding.

findings.attack_scenario: An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL logic into the ORDER BY clause to manipulate query results or access data.
findings.impact: Data manipulation, information disclosure, or denial of service via complex queries.
findings.recommendation: Validate the 'sort' parameter against a strict allow-list of permitted column names before use.

findings.title: SQL Injection in php-plain/search.php:14 via GET parameter 'cat'

evidence.why: Sink: User input interpolated directly into SQL string using heredoc syntax.

findings.attack_scenario: A crafted 'cat' parameter can alter the WHERE clause, bypassing category filters or injecting malicious SQL.
findings.impact: Unauthorized data access or modification based on database privileges.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or validate the 'cat' parameter against a strict allow-list of valid category values.

findings.title: SQL Injection in python-flask/app.py:12 via route parameter 'order_id'

evidence.why: Source: Route parameter (though type hint suggests integer, Flask passes it as string to the function unless explicitly cast).

evidence.code: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = %s" % order_id)
evidence.why: Sink: Variable interpolated into SQL string using Python's % formatting. While <int> hints exist, the variable passed to execute is not guaranteed to be a safe integer if the route logic or framework version allows bypass.

findings.attack_scenario: If the type hint <int> is not enforced strictly at runtime or if the parameter is manipulated before reaching this line, it can inject SQL.
findings.impact: Data access manipulation or injection of malicious SQL logic.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the parameter is explicitly cast to an integer before use, or better yet, rely on the framework's prepared statement handling if possible.

findings.title: SQL Injection in python-flask/app.py:29 via GET parameter 'q'

evidence.why: Source: User input from GET parameter

evidence.code: cur.execute(f"SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{q}%'")
evidence.why: Sink: User input interpolated directly into SQL query using f-string.

findings.attack_scenario: A crafted 'q' parameter can break the LIKE clause or inject SQL logic.
findings.impact: Data manipulation, information disclosure, or denial of service.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries (e.g., `cur.execute('...', ('%{q}%',))`) instead of f-strings.

findings.title: SQL Injection in sql-procs/sp_search_orders.sql:5 via parameter '@Sort'

evidence.code: SET @sql = 'SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE Customer = ''' + @Customer + ''' ORDER BY ' + @Sort
evidence.why: Sink: Parameter concatenated into dynamic SQL string.
Execution of the constructed dynamic SQL.

findings.attack_scenario: An attacker can pass a malicious string for '@Sort' to alter the query logic or access unauthorized columns.
findings.impact: Data manipulation, information disclosure, or denial of service.
findings.recommendation: Validate the '@Sort' parameter against a strict allow-list of permitted column names before constructing the SQL string.
